### TAG-181: Example 12.11 Controlled Fan-out Expression

**Status:** ✅ Implemented

## Software Notes

Good news: this one turns out not to need a parser or `rules.zig` change at all. The full expression already parses, and looking at the rule structure it builds, I think it actually *runs* correctly — the problem is narrower than that. Two things are happening:

**What** `.group`/`.mutex` means here. `Arg.kind == .group` with `.group.kind == .mutex` is the parser's representation of `({$out1 $out2 $out3 $out4})` — "exactly one of these fires." The four real names (`out1`..`out4`) live inside `dest[0].group.places`, not as top-level entries in `def.destinations`. `def.destinations` itself has exactly one synthetic entry with `.name = ""` standing in for the whole group. That's a legitimate, different-but-related shape to [TAG-142](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-142/example-123-further-abbreviated-expression-of-a-single-return-to-place)'s bare `<>` — not the same gap, just a sibling one.

**Why the rules should already work.** Contained definitions `A`/`B`/`C`/`D` go through the existing "fill-shaped children" path in `buildRules` (they have 0 sources, 0 destinations, one `.fill` statement each) — the same code path [TAG-177](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-177/example-1226-pure-value-expression-of-boolean-full-adder)'s `Z0[OUT<$Z0>]` uses. Each becomes a rule with `inputs = [contained.name]` (`"A"`, `"B"`, etc.) and `action = .copy_from("in")`. That's structurally identical to AND2's `p`/`q`/`r`/`s` dual-rail trick: seeding the `select` port with token `"A"` also seeds place `"A"` directly (via `Testbench`'s `env.seed(tok, tok)`), which fires that rule. So the actual value-flow logic looks like it needs zero changes.

**What's actually broken, in two places:**

1. `tb_vectors.resolve()` validates `@vectors` columns with `hasArg(def.destinations, c)`, which only checks direct names — it never looks inside a `.group`. That's the immediate cause of `BAD TB`.
2. `Testbench.run()`'s output-capture loop iterates `self.def.destinations` and does `env.get(dest.name)` — for the group entry, `dest.name` is `""`, so it silently never captures `out1`..`out4` even if step 1 is fixed. This one's subtler: it would have looked like `SUM/CARRY never valid`-style failures with no obvious cause.

Both fixes are additive and recurse through `PlaceGroup.places`, so nothing about AND2/FULLADD (plain, non-grouped destinations) changes.

`tb_vectors.zig` — replace the two `hasArg(...)` calls in `resolve()` with a group-aware version:

```
fn portExists(args: []const network.Arg, name: []const u8) bool {
    for (args) |arg| {
        if (arg.kind == .group) {
            if (arg.group) |g| {
                if (portExists(g.places, name)) return true;
            }
            continue;
        }
        if (std.mem.eql(u8, arg.name, name)) return true;
    }
    return false;
}
```

`testbench.zig` — replace the inline output-capture loop in `run()` with a recursive helper:

```
fn collectOutputs(
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    env: *Environment,
    args: []const network.Arg,
    outputs: *std.StringHashMapUnmanaged([]const u8),
) !void {
    for (args) |arg| {
        if (arg.kind == .group) {
            if (arg.group) |g| try collectOutputs(allocator, env, g.places, outputs);
            continue;
        }
        if (arg.name.len == 0) continue;
        switch (env.get(arg.name)) {
            .valid => |v| try outputs.put(allocator, arg.name, env.symbols.items[v]),
            .null_value => {},
        }
    }
}
```
